observation_summary: The method getLegendItems() in AbstractCategoryItemRenderer contained a logic error where it returned an empty collection if the dataset was NOT null, instead of returning it if the dataset WAS null. This caused the method to return an empty collection even when a valid dataset existed, leading to incorrect legend item counts.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing a conditional predicate from 'dataset != null' to 'dataset == null'. This is a classic error in conditional logic (a guard clause), which falls squarely under the 'Checking' category in ODC.
evidence_used: The bug report explicitly states: 'The variable dataset is guaranteed to be null in this location, I suppose that the check before that should actually read "if (dataset == null)", not "if (dataset != null)".'
The fix_diff_oracle shows the change: '- if (dataset != null) {' to '+ if (dataset == null) {'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic is part of a method, the root cause is specifically an incorrect conditional guard, which is the definition of Checking.
